scope: scripts/qualify_interruption.py on a Debug build of 61f75b8 frozen with git archive, 16 of 16 cases, each in its own owned Portal on an owned copy of TinyMySQLClient_V15.ap15 (project folder, OpenWithUpgrade, pf-*) or TinyMySQLClient_V14_1.zap14 (archive, RetrieveWithUpgrade, pa-*), reconciled once by engineering_admission_reconcile from a fresh Host. Worker and owned TIA terminated at the first dispatchIntent (int: destination never created) -> released, source and destination unchanged; at receipt copying (cpy) and upgrading (upg, inside the native upgrade) -> held with the partial owned copy; at the first .ap21 at the observed layout while the receipt is upgrading (prj) -> held without the project being opened. Host stopped after the durable dispatch intent and before dispatch (hint, host.project_upgrade.beforeDispatch) -> released unchanged. Host killed at receipt copying (hcpy) and upgrading (hupg), and Host stopped after the native upgrade returned but before recording it (hret, host.project_upgrade) -> the worker finished, released with the destination verifiedApplied, and the reconciled V21 project (TinyMySQLClient_V15_V21, TinyMySQLClient_V14_V21) opened in the same fresh session with its pinned inventory (17 hardware items, 1 PLC, 7 blocks, 0 inconsistent). Every case: source copy fingerprint unchanged and proven unchanged by the reconciler, exactly one project_upgrade admission and at most one destination (no replay), destination unchanged by reconciliation, each held admission keeps its source reserved (a second project_upgrade is refused ResourceBusy). Originals byte-identical before and after; copies removed; no run file names a folder above an original.
limitations: Interruption is process termination of the worker with its owned TIA, or Host loss by kill or a qualification Host point, once per case; power loss, disk faults and remote transport are not exercised.

Two small public examples (a V15 project folder and a V14 SP1 archive). Boundaries are observed through the durable upgrade receipt and admission store; the copy of these examples takes milliseconds, so each case records the durable state it hit (all 16 hit their intended state).
A partial copy or unfinished upgrade stays held; releasing it needs someone to remove the owned destination and reconcile again, which is not exercised.

Reconciliation trusts the worker-written upgrade receipt once it is bound to the recomputed source hash and the observed layout; a receipt edited inside the owned artifacts tree after the interruption is trusted.
